Subject: Coalesced bundle idea — seeking clarification on upgrade steps

Hi Karthik / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked the latency/throughput profiles you showed and think Redwood could fit our production needs. Before we get teams aligned, I want to run one idea by you so procurement and product can scope the contract properly.

Current thinking at Clearline: we want a single, coalesced "AI Bundles" approach rather than many small add-ons — simpler billing and a clearer upgrade path as usage grows. The sticking points for us are:
- whether features can be "opted into" within a bundle (e.g., reranker + embeddings only turned on for select routes) without full-tier migration;
- how proration and seat vs throughput accounting works when we step customers up mid-cycle; and
- whether Redwood can offer a short pilot window with negotiated pricing that converts cleanly into a committed tier.

I've attached a short requirements doc that lists the Clearline features we care about and expected monthly token footprint. Could you confirm whether that model fits a coalesced bundle approach or if we should stick with a la carte modules?

Thanks,
Clara Singh
Head of AI Product, Clearline AI
clara@clearline.ai

Hi Clara — really appreciate the doc and the clear priorities.

On Fri, Jun 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM Clara Singh <clara@clearline.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked the latency/throughput profiles you showed...

Short answer: yes, we can support a coalesced bundle approach, but there are trade-offs we should outline so procurement and product can sign off quickly. Below is a pragmatic stepwise proposal for Clearline that balances billing simplicity with the per-route feature opt-in you mentioned.

1) Bundle structure (proposed)
- Core Bundle (Base): embeddings, standard generation, basic SLOs — priced per-unit.
- Accelerator Add-on: reranking, conv-cache, response-format enforcement — purchased as a single add-on SKU but toggleable per-route.
- Enterprise Ops: dedicated throughput buckets, private VPC option, extended retention/audit logs.

2) Opt-in mechanics
- Features in Accelerator Add-on can be toggled at the API route level. Billing for the add-on is on the bundle account, but we meter per-route usage for internal visibility. This preserves simple invoices while giving product owners control.

3) Upgrade/proration behavior
- If Clearline upgrades mid-cycle, we prorate the committed capacity (pro-rata credits applied to future invoices) and keep add-on usage billed at usage rates until the new tier's committed capacity is provisioned (usually within 24–48 hours).

4) Pilot & conversion terms
- We can run a 6-week pilot with a capped pilot rate and convert to a committed tier with a 10% introductory credit applied to the first 3 months upon commitment. The pilot MOU outlines scope, pass/fail metrics, and conversion mechanics.

I've attached a simple bundle matrix to illustrate quantities and price brackets. If it helps, we can run a 30-minute pricing workshop with Product + Procurement to map your exact routes to the bundle toggles.

Next steps I propose:
- Jonas and I review the requirements doc against telemetry to size the Accelerator SKU (we'll come back with exact quantities).
- Schedule a 30-min workshop (link below).
- Draft pilot MOU if Clearline wants to move forward.

Meeting: https://meet.redwood.ai/s/6a8b-workshop

Thanks Karthik, this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement/product before we book the workshop:

- Feature opt-in at route level is exactly what we need, but we need per-feature usage caps to be enforceable (so product owners don’t accidentally blow our pilot budget). Can the Accelerator SKU expose hard caps?
- Pilot conversion: the 10% introductory credit is fine, but procurement prefers the credit applied as a one-time invoice credit rather than stretched across months. Is that possible?
- Discount ask: if we commit to a 12-week pilot with a clear conversion window and a first-year commitment (12 months post-conversion), would Redwood consider a 15% introductory discount to the Enterprise Ops tier for the first 6 months? We have a deadline of June 30 to get procurement approvals for the pilot spend.

If you can answer those three points we’ll pull procurement and legal onto the 30-min slot.

Hi Megan — quick answers and next steps so we can hit your June 30 procurement gate: 

1) Hard caps: yes — Accelerator SKU can be configured with hard per-feature caps at the account level (we’ll surface alerts and reject requests once caps are exceeded). We’ll document the enforcement behavior in the pilot MOU.

2) Credit mechanics: we can apply the introductory credit as a one-time invoice credit upon conversion (rather than spreading it). Finance (cc’d: Lauren) confirms mechanics are straightforward for the pilot->commit flow.

3) Discount: we can extend a 15% introductory discount to the Enterprise Ops tier for the first 6 months provided Clearline signs the pilot MOU by June 30 and commits to a 12-month term upon conversion. Ben — if finance/legal flags anything material, please advise.
